skills.name: Economic systems: the basic allocation questions

note.text: An economic system organises how resources are owned, production is coordinated and output is distributed. Every society faces what to produce, how to produce and for whom to produce. What concerns the goods and services chosen. How concerns methods and resource combinations. For whom concerns who receives output and on what basis. These questions arise because resources are scarce. A system's label alone does not tell us whether every outcome is fair or efficient.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: An economic system organises how resources are owned, production is coordinated and output is distributed. Every society faces what to produce, how to produce and for whom to produce. What concerns the goods and services chosen. How concerns methods and resource combinations. For whom concerns who receives output and on what basis. These questions arise because resources are scarce. A system's label alone does not tell us whether every outcome is fair or efficient.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: A community near Buea may decide whether land should support food crops or housing. That is a what question. Choosing hand tools or machinery concerns how. Deciding who receives housing or can buy food concerns for whom. A single project can involve all these questions, but they remain analytically different.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify what decision is being made before naming the question. Look for product, method or recipient. Do not turn a question about production technique into one about ownership without evidence. Systems can combine different ways of answering the allocation questions.

key_words.meaning: which goods and services to make
which techniques and resource combinations to use
who receives output and on what basis
assigning scarce resources among competing uses

examples: A community chooses between a clinic building and a market shelter.
A farmer chooses between hand tools and a hired machine.
A housing scheme decides which households qualify.
